extracted.intended_audience: USPTO staff, patent examiners, patent practitioners, applicants, patent stakeholders (inventors, businesses, law firms, academics)
extracted.subtask_description: A preliminary USPTO/PPAC framework describing principles, measurable metrics, process changes, and pilot ideas to improve patent quality across search, examination, applications, administrative processes, tools, and training. Intended to structure roundtable discussion and public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent quality definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions which increase the likelihood that claims granted by the USPTO are legally valid plus actions which reduce the likelihood that valid claims are not improperly rejected by the USPTO. Divided by timeliness (actions which increase process efficiency and reduce overall application pendency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent quality does not include a legal determination of eligibility of any particular technology, economic contribution of an invention, or patent procurement cost; applies to all statutory eligible inventions equally. Cost impacts of proposed procedural changes must be factored into fee/implementation decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness as part of quality (reduce pendency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeliness (reducing overall pendency from filing to final disposition) is an element of patent quality and should be pursued alongside accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness is not inapposite to improving quality: can do both by removing inefficiencies. Ultimate/Stretch goals suggested: FOAM in 6 months, overall pendency 18 months, no significant backlog.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial substantive areas for improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Five focus areas for improving patent quality: The Search; The Examination; The Application; Administrative efficiencies; Training and Education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The public comment period focused on search, examination and application; administrative efficiencies includes electronic conversion, auditing, performance tracking, and transparency. Appeals/reexaminations acknowledged but reserved for later analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough, accurate and timely examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The public and the applicant deserve a thorough, accurate and timely examination of each application they pay to file and have examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each application is potentially important regardless of business model or technology. Examiner and supervisory quality must be considered alongside production metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhaust and enforce existing rules; pilot process changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimize by exhausting existing rules and procedures, enforcing existing rules, and piloting process changes with a 'do no harm' mindset while identifying potential statutory/substantive rule changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on procedural simplification and information technology; avoid introducing unintended consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality review should address three core failure modes
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality review should address: 1) an incorrect understanding of the scope of the invention; 2) an incorrect understanding of the prior art; and 3) an incorrect application of the law or procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process and training interventions should be targeted to these specific causes of poor outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentivize best practices for applicants and PTO staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Create incentives and review performance to encourage accuracy, efficiency and effective collaboration between applicants/practitioners and PTO staff (examiners, supervisors, group directors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process metrics should include incentives for applicants who follow best practices; examiner performance should include process and result metrics as well as production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance metrics to avoid gaming
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics must be balanced because focusing on one metric (e.g., incorrect issuances) can produce undesired behavior (e.g., reduced issuances increasing incorrect rejections) and vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select metrics that encourage desired behaviors and monitor for unintended consequences (analysis paralysis from too many metrics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmark against other patent offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Use benchmarking against leading patent offices (e.g., EPO, JPO) to identify best practices and harmonize where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmarking supports work sharing and harmonization of patentability standards; consider EPO and other offices' classification/search practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doing it right the first time
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasize minimizing errors, rework, and delays by moving resources and prioritization to early stages, reducing premature final rejections, unnecessary appeals and continuing applications (RCEs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct in-process quality reviews earlier, measure critical process points, use metrics for continuous improvement, and make data publicly available for transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align examiner production count with performance and process efficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Further align the Examiner Production count system with performance and process efficiencies so examiners are not penalized for spending time on quality activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give examiners appropriate time to do their jobs well; do not confuse quality with mere production counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous measurement and feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality improvement is an ongoing process: measure results, use feedback from measures to make additional changes, and treat quality improvement as continuous (quality improvement does not equal perfection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use metrics to guide interventions and refine them iteratively; avoid excessive metrics that cause analysis paralysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early in-process quality reviews and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct quality reviews earlier in the process and measure and publish critical process points and results to enable continuous improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make data and measures publicly available in real time to identify effective changes and next opportunities for improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant responsibility to improve quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants have responsibility to improve patent quality by filing well-prepared specifications and claims; the PTO cannot produce high-quality patents from poor-quality applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incentivize applicant pre-filing search and clarity; consider mechanisms (preliminary searches, advisory actions) to improve application quality before full examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metrics selection principles
rubrics_metrics.description: To improve quality, select metrics that measure the right things: measure most important areas for improvement and encourage desired behaviors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid too many metrics; prioritize clear, public, and real-time metrics that reveal what works and what doesn't.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish process metrics and result metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Process metrics focus on reducing errors and improving timeliness (efficiency); result metrics focus on the ultimate quality of PTO determinations (effectiveness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner performance should include both types as well as production metrics; process metrics should include applicant incentives for following best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current PTO quality metrics (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: List of existing or proposed PTO metrics: Pendency to first office action on merits (FOAM); Classification Accuracy; Allowance rate and allowance compliance review; Backlog of unexamined applications; First office allowance; In process review; Interviews and 'compact prosecution'; RCEs; Final rejection data; Examiner performance (QIR); Examiner count system; Overtime and telework; New examiner hiring and retention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These metrics are examples for monitoring; careful selection and balancing of such metrics is required to avoid perverse incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTO strategic and ultimate quality goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Targets proposed for performance: strategic goals (e.g., FOAM 10.7 months; overall pendency 24 months; reduce backlog) and ultimate/stretch goals (FOAM 6 months; overall pendency 18 months; no significant backlog; significantly reduce RCE trend; 100% PTO decisions affirmed by BPAI and Federal Circuit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ultimate goals are customer-driven and should not be driven solely by PTO personnel management concerns; proposed timelines (e.g., applicant should know allowance/appeal status by 18 months) are guidance for process design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search: identify closest prior art promptly and comprehensively
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality requires that the closest prior art relevant to determining patentability, clarity and scope of claims is identified and properly evaluated as soon as possible; the search must be comprehensive and done preferably only once per application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must have ample time and credit for the search; time studies by technology area may be needed to determine adequate search time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner responsibility to identify, apply and explain prior art findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners have primary responsibility to identify, apply and clearly explain either why a claim is valid/allowable or should be rejected in view of the closest prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office Actions should clearly articulate pertinence of cited portions and provide guidance for applicants where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper classification prior to search
rubrics_metrics.description: Proper classification before search aids examiners and improves comprehensiveness and timeliness of searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider outsourcing classification if accurate; start classification sooner; make classification transparent to applicants; defined terms in the specification aid classification. Consider adopting or integrating EPC, FI/F-Terms, DEKLA, Derwent codes for improved coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary classification and search of provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider classifying, reviewing for 35 U.S.C. §112 compliance, and performing a preliminary contractor search on provisional applications (if applicant provides a representative claim), providing non-binding advisory advice to applicant and examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charge a fee equal to cost of advisory action (creditable to later filing fee); advisory action could highlight deficiencies early and reduce later rework/backlog.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. §112 review to aid search
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity of claimed invention and adequacy of written description and antecedent basis aid the search; pre-search review for §112 compliance (original or provisional) could identify undefined/inconsistent terms and deficiencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An advisory action on provisional could notify applicant of deficiencies within ~8 months to permit corrective action in the original application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive search and gap analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Search quality requires comprehensive search coverage, including foreign language literature and non-public prior art (e.g., offers for sale/on-sale bars), and a gap analysis identifying what types of prior art are missed by searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform time studies by technology area, categorize missed prior art by tech area, benchmark with other offices, and apply search quality metrics to examiner performance. Examiner must read the entire application before search/exam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand and improve search techniques, software and work-sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Address and expand existing databases, search techniques (e.g., semantic/concept algorithms), partner with private search engines, and accelerate international work-sharing (automatic electronic provision of search results among offices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider 'intent to file' forms to enable worksharing, PCT/PPA mechanisms, and use data from PPH to reduce rework and pendency. Speed transfer of prior art uncovered by counterpart offices directly between offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party search assistance and specialist search examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider third-party assistance (e.g., Peer-to-Patent/wiki), incentive mechanisms/bounties for prior art submission, use of search-specialist examiners with advanced search/software expertise, and partnerships with private search firms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer-to-patent feedback may help guide examiners but scaling is uncertain; third-party submissions could be allowed with strict format (identify claim elements and specific wording/figures relevant) and limited/no arguments to avoid examiner burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open source prior art indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: Index and archive public open source software projects and their revision history so examiners can identify relevant open source code as prior art at specific dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create searchable indexes (e.g., snapshot by date) and integrate open-source repositories (sourceforge, etc.) into examiner search tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Disclosure Statement (IDS) usage and Rule 56 considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether IDS aids examiner search; analyze why examiners may not utilize IDS (time/credits); consider changing Rule 56 to limit IDS to non-public prior art and create incentives for disclosure of non-public prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explore methods to more efficiently analyze large numbers of applicant-supplied references and expand training for examiners and applicants on how to use searching and disclosures effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentivize applicant pre-filing searches and low-cost advisory searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage and/or require applicant pre-filing submissions (e.g., a one-paragraph summary, up to 10 claims) for a low-cost search by the Office, producing a simple opinion (e.g., X/Y/A ratings) and possibly granting special status to participating applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such processes could be required or incentivized and fees could be credited toward later filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner search performance metrics and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure examiner search performance (time studies, credits for search), create pre-examiner search interviews, and provide reporting of search results to applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incentivize accurate, thorough searches and facilitate early applicant-examiner collaboration to reduce rework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination: technical accuracy & supervisory oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure technical accuracy in examination with pilot programs (e.g., ombudsman), robust examiner and supervisor performance reviews, and defined roles for supervisors and quality review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supervisor and quality review roles should be strengthened; examiner and supervisor quality performance is as important as production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough first Office Action on the Merits (FAOM) and reduce premature finals
rubrics_metrics.description: Strive for thorough first Office Actions on the merits to minimize premature final rejections and unnecessary appeals or RCEs; focus resources early to reduce pendency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to provide FOAM in a target timeframe and give examiners appropriate time/credit to produce comprehensive first actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of interviews, compact prosecution and pre-appeal conferencing
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage interviews (first office action interviews), compact prosecution techniques, and pilot pre-appeal brief conferences to resolve issues earlier and reduce pendency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track interview outcomes and implement 'compact prosecution' practices where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage RCEs and reasons for allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce unnecessary Requests for Continued Examination (RCEs) and clarify reasons for allowance (e.g., per MPEP 1302.14) to improve final disposition accuracy and reduce trend of repeat work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze RCE trends, address drivers of RCE filings, and implement process changes to reduce reliance on RCEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application quality: defining terms and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear definition of terms in the specification and consistent application formatting improve examination quality and search/classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage applicants to define terms, use consistent terminology and follow standardized formats; consider guidance on standard algorithms and support for claim language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative efficiencies, data transparency and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve administrative efficiencies (electronic procedures, auditing, performance tracking), collect high-quality data, and implement stages of monitoring and review supported by tools and software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make data publicly available to promote transparency; harmonize electronic filing forms and invest in administrative software and portals that support quality metrics collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tools to assist examiners and improve data collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and evaluate tools (commercial and in-house) to assist examiners: concept/semantic search algorithms, context-aware navigation linking claims/spec/figures, URL naming schemes, harmonized filing forms, checklists, and text-to-speech functionality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tools can reduce examiner burden and improve understanding of scope; modify office action forms and PAIR portals to enhance structured data collection (e.g., standardized checkboxes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and cross-education
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage the patent community to create cross-training programs for applicants, practitioners and examiners; establish continuing education for practitioners (CEP) and rigorous examiner training and legal education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEP modules should be accessible and printable; training could include mentoring, use of retired examiners as trainers, negotiation/communication skills, industry-specific seminars, and cross-training to foster common understanding of technology and terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surveys tied to real-time application experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct surveys connected to real-time experience per application to gather targeted feedback on quality of examination, understanding of invention, administrative processes (interviews, restriction practice, RCEs, pre-appeal conferences), and other programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveys should be anonymized, publicly available, and used to focus examiner training and evaluate policies; ensure surveyors are authorized by the Office for credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample survey evaluation questions (MPEP/legal compliance focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey questions should probe whether examiners consistently follow required legal frameworks and MPEP guidance for rejections under 35 U.S.C. §§ 101, 102, 103, and 112 (e.g., follow flowcharts, consider all claim language, show technical reasoning for inherency, follow rationales for obviousness, make enablement/showings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use such targeted questions to evaluate corps-wide consistency without focusing on individual examiners when respondents may be reluctant to identify specific examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Quality Index (PQI) and correlates of validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop metrics (e.g., Patent Quality Index) that evaluate characteristics associated with validity; examples include closeness of claims to specification and the quality of applicant/examiner prior art identification and use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PQI to identify problematic aspects of the process, automate evaluation, identify critical steps in examination, and guide targeted improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated textual analysis and standardized reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use automated textual analysis and standardized checklists/check-boxes in PAIR for types of rejections to permit large-scale statistical evaluation of bases for actions without manual coding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardization enables reporting by art unit, examiner, or time period and supports process-feedback control mechanisms to improve quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track examiner communications that do not help move case forward
rubrics_metrics.description: Track and analyze examiner responses which fail to indicate how an applicant can move the case forward or otherwise capture instances where examiners assert there is nothing that could be done to put the case in condition for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality assurance should focus on such cases as they likely capture situations of 'ships passing in the night' and provide insight into process failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance focus on actionable suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality assurance processes should emphasize cases where the examiner offers no suggestions for allowable subject matter or claim amendments, as these may indicate poor prosecution communication or inadequate examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze these cases and provide feedback/training to reduce occurrences; encourage examiners to offer potential resolutions where appropriate.
